title: csvread
summary: Read numeric data from CSV files in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Performs host-side file I/O and parsing, and results remain on the CPU. Public host controls do not involve an acceleration provider; with the `csvread-resident-control-inputs` extension enabled, resident controls are gathered through their owning provider before parsing.

description: `csvread(filename)` reads real or complex numeric data from comma-separated text files and returns a dense double matrix. Row and column controls are zero-based.
behaviors: Accepts character vectors or string scalars for the file name. String arrays must contain exactly one element.
`csvread(filename, row, col)` starts reading at the zero-based row `row` and column `col`, skipping any data before that offset.

`csvread(filename, row, col, range)` reads only the rectangle described by `range`. The public forms are a four-element numeric range `[r1 c1 r2 c2]` or an A1 range such as `"B2..D6"`. RunMat's colon-separated A1 range and two-element numeric range are independent compatibility-gated extensions.
Empty fields (two consecutive commas or a trailing comma) are interpreted as `0`. Tokens such as `NaN`, `Inf`, and `-Inf` are accepted (case-insensitive).
Any other nonnumeric token raises an error that identifies the offending row and column.
File input is read as byte-oriented CSV text before numeric parsing, so non-UTF-8 bytes in skipped header rows or skipped label columns do not cause an I/O decoding failure.

Real input produces a dense double tensor; any complex token (`a+bi`, `a+bj`, or a pure-imaginary form) produces a complex-double tensor without discarding an all-zero imaginary component. An empty file produces a `0×0` tensor.
Paths can contain `~` to reference the home directory; RunMat expands the token before opening the file.

faqs.question: Why does `csvread` complain about text data?
faqs.answer: `csvread` is limited to numeric CSV content. If a field contains letters, quoted strings, or other tokens that cannot be parsed as numbers, the builtin raises an error. Switch to `readmatrix` or `readtable` when the file mixes text and numbers.

faqs.question: Are the row and column offsets zero-based?
faqs.answer: Yes. `csvread(filename, row, col)` treats `row` and `col` as zero-based counts to skip from the start of the file before reading results.

faqs.question: How are Excel-style ranges interpreted?
faqs.answer: The public A1 form uses two dots, for example `"B2..D5"`, with 1-based row numbers and column letters. RunMat also accepts colon syntax such as `"B2:D5"` only when the `csvread-colon-range` extension is enabled. Both forms include their endpoints.

faqs.question: Can I read files with quoted numeric fields?
faqs.answer: Yes. A field wrapped in double quotes is parsed as a numeric token; general quoted-field CSV escaping is outside `csvread`'s narrow numeric format.

faqs.question: What happens to empty cells?
faqs.answer: Empty cells (two consecutive commas or a trailing delimiter) become zero, matching MATLAB's `csvread` behaviour.

faqs.question: Does `csvread` support custom delimiters?
faqs.answer: No. `csvread` always uses comma separation. Use `dlmread` or `readmatrix` for other delimiters.

faqs.question: How do I keep the results on the GPU?
faqs.answer: `csvread` returns a host tensor. Call `gpuArray(csvread(...))` after reading, or prefer `readmatrix` with `'Like', gpuArray.zeros(1)` to keep residency on the GPU automatically.

faqs.question: What if the file is empty?
faqs.answer: An empty file results in a `0×0` double tensor. MATLAB behaves the same way.

faqs.question: Does `csvread` change the working directory?
faqs.answer: No. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory and do not modify it.

gpu_residency: `csvread` always returns a host-resident tensor because it performs file I/O and parsing on the CPU. Resident filename, offset, and range controls are accepted only when the `csvread-resident-control-inputs` RunMat extension is enabled.
gpu_behavior: `csvread` performs file I/O and parsing on the host CPU. Public host controls require no provider. With the `csvread-resident-control-inputs` extension enabled, resident controls are gathered through their owning provider; the resulting tensor still returns in host memory.
